subject: dsa
title: Top K Frequent Elements
summary: Count each value, then bucket the values by how often they occur. Scanning buckets from the highest frequency down gives the top k without ever sorting.
problem: Return the k values that appear most often in nums.

steps.caption: We want the k = 2 most frequent values in [1,1,1,2,2,3]. First, count how often each value appears.
One pass builds the counts: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears twice, 3 once.
Sorting by count is O(n log n). Instead bucket by frequency: position f holds the values seen f times. With n=6 elements, frequencies run 0 to 6.
Drop each value into its frequency bucket: 3 occurs once goes to bucket 1, 2 occurs twice goes to bucket 2, 1 occurs 3 times goes to bucket 3.
Now scan buckets from the highest frequency down, collecting values until we have k=2. Buckets 6, 5, 4 are empty.
Bucket 3 holds value 1 — the most frequent. Take it. Collected so far: [1].
Bucket 2 holds value 2. Take it. Collected: [1, 2] — that's k=2, so we can stop.
The two most frequent elements are [1, 2] — found in O(n) with counting and buckets, no sort.
